headline: Consumer Reports Rates Apocalypse Kits for High-Stakes Intersection Negotiations
deck: Urbanites now face delays in both life and death as unyielding traffic stalemates take center stage.
article:
Consumer Reports has issued its 2026 star ratings for apocalypse evacuation kits built for multi-hour intersection negotiations. Wildfires near Bordeaux have jammed every exit route, turning routine merges into endurance contests where drivers trade right-of-way claims like livestock at auction.

The DMV-issued yield-priority maps earned five stars for their HOA-approved snack compartments. "A granola bar settles more disputes than any horn," said traffic mediator Douglas Mirth.

Roundabout arbitration tents scored 4.5 stars thanks to built-in coffee and clipboard slots. Semaphore glove sets managed only three stars after one pair shredded during a 47-car standoff at Fifth and Maple.

Local surveys show 79 percent of residents would rather circle forever than repeat last week’s deadlock at Pine and Elm.
author: Evelyn P. Exclamation, Senior Roadway Negotiation Analyst

oped.title: Consumer Reports Misses the Hat of the Matter
oped.author: Lord Percival Brimsworth, Grand Arbiter of Eternal Roundabouts and Proprietor of Brimsworth's Indispensable Negotiation Millinery
oped.body: Consumer Reports again rates kits while ignoring the true culprit: inadequate headwear at every roundabout. These urbanites stall not from fatigue but from last season’s fedoras that broadcast weakness and invite gridlock. My Brimsworth Crown, fitted with semaphore feathers, clears any standoff in under four hours, yet sales lag because buyers blame missing traffic lights instead of their own millinery. Mandate the $189 chapeau at every crossing and both life and death would run on schedule. Until then I yield to no lesser hat and no report that overlooks my invention.

classifieds.text: Lightly dented 2025 Apocalypse Kit, rated #1 by Consumer Reports for 14-hour roundabout negotiations. Includes folding gavel, tear-gas flares, and three days of energy gels. Must sell before my lease at the Elm & Vine deadlock expires.
Wanted: calm, well-spoken negotiator to stand in for me at the Main & 9th stalemate weekdays 7-9 a.m. Prior experience with four-way Mexican standoffs preferred. $45/hr plus hazard gas coupons.
Lost at the Oak roundabout Tuesday: my dignity, one white flag, and a half-eaten protein bar. If found, please return to the silver Prius still waiting to merge; no questions asked.
To the guy in the lifted truck who wouldn’t yield at Pine & 12th: sorry I called your mother a roundabout. Coffee at the next neutral intersection? Must be willing to blink first.

panels.caption: Driver at gridlocked roundabout waves Consumer Reports: "This 'Negotiator Deluxe' kit only scores 2/5—says it fails once someone pulls a gun over right-of-way."
Passenger flips page: "The top-rated model adds a megaphone and liability waivers, but reviewers note it still loses to the guy with bigger tires."
Both cars remain frozen as a third vehicle claims the circle: "Review update: all kits rated 'posthumous' pending actual movement."

stories.headline: BunkerReady Shares Climb as Negotiation Kits Top Quarterly Sales
stories.deck: Arbitration tents now bundled with every six-pack of bottled water at suburban warehouses.
stories.article:
BunkerReady Inc. logged a 412 percent surge in intersection kit shipments after commuters began ordering extra signal paddles and stalemate forms for ordinary errands. Strip-mall distribution centers installed dedicated loading lanes once delivery trucks started trapping themselves at the gates.

The flagship kit now ships with a laminated HOA priority chart that cuts average standoff time from 47 minutes to 19. Sales analysts attribute the gains to clearer paperwork rather than improved driver manners.

real_world_echo: Wildfire evacuation near Bordeaux, mirrored as urbanites fleeing 'walls of stalled vehicles' at uncontrolled intersections rather than flames
